reconstructed_steps.text: Use an ACTUAL smooth projective curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued field C, with valuation ring V and residue field kappa. For genus zero the actual split projective line and its standard Gauss model give the initial semistable model. For positive genus use BL85 Theorem7.1, whose printed statement and proof were previously read, and the actual model/skeleton correspondence BPR4.11 with its printed proof4.15. BPR4.22 explicitly works over a non-Noetherian rank-one valuation ring, not merely a complete discrete valuation ring. Its proof refers out to stable reduction; no claim to have independently reconstructed every recursive external proof.

BPR3.13(2) puts any prescribed finite set of actual type-II points into a semistable vertex set containing the old set. BPR3.13(3) additionally separates any finite set of classical punctures into distinct open-ball components. BPR4.8 says these punctures reduce to distinct SMOOTH points. Refine loop edges once to obtain strong semistability. BPR4.9 gives each actual edge length val(a_e) in Gamma_C and4.10 identifies the actual formal skeleton with the analytic one. Refinements retain every old cycle. Union of the two prescribed finite vertex sets supplies a common refinement. These are actual models for this curve, rather than a graph independently declared realizable.

Every affine chart of a BPR admissible model is A=V<T_1,...,T_r>/I, V-flat with I FINITELY GENERATED. Choose b with0<|b|<1. In V<T>/b^n every restricted series reduces to a polynomial because only finitely many coefficients survive; the kernel is b^n V<T>, since dividing the coefficients by the fixed b^n still makes them tend to zero. Thus A/b^n A is a finitely presented algebra over V/b^n, defined by the finitely many reduced generators of I. V-flatness of A gives flatness of A/b^n A over V/b^n. This verifies the flat finite-presentation reductions required in238 without assuming that V or V/b^n is Noetherian.

Spec(V/b^n) has just one prime. For x in the maximal ideal of V, rank one implies x^r lies in b^n V for some r; hence m_V/b^n is a nil ideal, though generally not a nilpotent ideal of bounded order. The residue-field base change of the reduction X_n is the actual proper semistable special fibre. Since X_n is locally of finite presentation by A3, Stacks37.3.4(8), tag0BPG, applies to this arbitrary thickening and proves X_n proper. The printed proof invokes37.3.1: underlying universal homeomorphisms preserve quasi-compactness, universal closedness and separation. No finite-order nilpotence has been substituted here. Properness of the formal model/special fibre itself is part of the actual proper model fromA1.

A prospective way to supply the initial SAME-BUNDLE formal extension avoids asserting domination of an unrelated projective reference model. Choose an integral multiple m0L and a nonzero actual meromorphic section sigma. Its divisor has finite classical support on the actual algebraic curve. Also choose a finite basepoint-free family defining an equal-weight pure FS reference theta and include the zeros and poles of every algebraic ratio s_i/sigma in the puncture set. Adapt an ACTUAL semistable model by A2. Every puncture lies over a different smooth point, so its bounded evaluation on a formal affine chart maps A to V and supplies a section Spf(V) of the formal model. Properness supplies a unique global reduction; on the smooth chart the compatible reductions are sections of a smooth relative curve.

For each n the image of this section in the smooth locus of X_n is an effective relative Cartier divisor. Stacks44.3.1, tag0B9D, gives this for arbitrary bases: a section is finite locally free of degree one, hence Cartier. Stacks31.23.8, tag067R, also gives its regular immersion. The compatible Cartier ideals locally have compatible generators; a local smooth coordinate t centered at the puncture gives the equation t-t(p), and its derivative is a unit. The ratio of any two such generators is a formal unit. Their compatible inverse-limit invertible ideals define a formal Cartier divisor. This last compatibility/local-coordinate application must be written in full in a eventual paper; the scheme lemma alone has not been silently promoted to a formal effectiveness grant. Taking the signed horizontal divisor associated to div(sigma) gives a formal line bundle with generic fibre m0L and the generic identification specified by sigma.

On a node annulus avoiding all punctures, each actual rational ratio s_i/sigma is an analytic unit. BPR2.13 and5.15(1)-(2) make its logarithmic norm factor through the actual retraction and affine with integer slope. On an unpunctured open ball its norm is constant. On a ball containing puncture p, a smooth formal parameter t centered at p and the horizontal bundle frame remove the order of sigma; every section has nonnegative residual order j_i at p, with at least one j_i=0 because the family has no common zero. The remaining analytic unit has constant norm. The reference weight relative to that frame is therefore the maximum of finitely many affine functions log|c_i|+j_i log|t|, divided by the bundle multiple. It is constant sufficiently far toward p, because a zero-order section dominates after the last crossing. Crossings occur at Gamma_C values since Gamma_C is divisible. Thus only finitely many additional actual type-II vertices are required.

Consequently theta relative to the horizontal formal bundle is an ACTUAL continuous finite Gamma_C-valued PL function with rational slopes on a finite core, constant on every attached formal fibre. Apply241 C2-C5 to that finite actual model: meromorphic equations c_v and c_v*x^k, norm-one scalar transition factors, and branchwise degree computation construct a global vertical Cartier twist. Its metric is exactly the original genuine pure FS reference, with its SAME specified algebraic generic bundle. This route replaces the unverified reference-domination premise of241 C1. It still needs the complete compatible horizontal-divisor construction A6 and the raw curvature/component-degree identification for this exact model, rather than merely an abstract graph recognition.

STRICT-POSITIVITY CORRECTION:238 F10 and241 C8 described adding a fraction of the original reference curvature as if that by itself made every component degree strictly positive. This is insufficient on new components with reference degree zero. The ACTUAL235 Theorem1 proof instead starts on the entire finite vertex set with rho=(V/k)*sum_v delta_v and mu_epsilon=(1-epsilon)*mu+epsilon*rho. Every old vertex, including vertices added by previous refinement or loop subdivision, has a positive target margin. It then chooses shared Gamma_C vertex heights and rational slopes bracketing each chord, with a movable UPWARD bend on every edge. The inserted bend has strictly positive mass; sufficiently small slope errors preserve the margin at all old vertices. This is the required construction. No additional zero-degree vertex may be introduced after this positivity step without repeating it on the enlarged graph.

On the exact semistable model realizing all original vertices and movable bends,241 computes the component degrees of the twisted actual bundle as m*(theta_v+Delta h(v)). With the corrected235 construction, ALL component degrees are strictly positive. A3-A4 verify the proper flat finitely presented reductions; fibre ampleness follows on the actual proper special curve. Apply238 with cutoff d0>=1 to algebraize that exact compatible polarized pair. Its generic analytic pair is unchanged only after applying the actual completion/generic-fibre comparison for a proper finitely presented V-scheme and proper rigid GAGA; BPR4.2(2) names Conrad1999 Theorem5.3.1(4). Its primary proof is the next reading obligation, not claimed read in this record. Relative ampleness then supplies high globally generated powers and BE5.14 recognizes the same bundle metric as pure FS. The limit of these genuinely recognized approximants, not the numerical positivity condition alone, supplies a prospective continuous atomic metric.

No original closes here. To complete the actual all-genus equation, still prove all formal/generic/SAME-BUNDLE identifications, the raw curvature and kernel-test applications, and the all-point finite-energy operator/Green-integral construction in235. Terminal values and type-III interior continuity must be checked on the actual charts as in241. Finite Galois orbits may be obtained from the actual invariant pure-FS measure support as in240, but averaging arbitrary singular noninvariant potentials remains disallowed. The original arbitrary-dimensional P16.4 equation and attainment remain separate open requirements.
